prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1107; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver regarding a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle stopped abruptly and was struck from behind. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles uploaded to the file.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant. Reports neck and upper back pain beginning the day after the collision, consistent with whiplash. Claimant states she sought care at an urgent care clinic and was given a referral to a physical therapist. Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Explained the claims process and the right to seek legal counsel at any time.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage appraisal completed for the insured vehicle. Rear bumper, trunk lid, and tail light assembly damaged. Repair estimate received from the preferred shop. Rental coverage confirmed under the policy for the duration of repairs, subject to policy limits.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the urgent care clinic. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain with soft tissue injury. Treatment plan includes physical therapy sessions twice weekly for six weeks. Records reviewed and placed in the injury file. Requested authorization from claimant to obtain prior records for the past five years to assess any pre-existing neck complaints.

Entry 5: Claimant returned the medical authorization form. Physical therapy progress notes requested. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the ongoing treatment plan. File flagged for follow-up in thirty days or upon receipt of the therapy discharge summary.
